arxiv-1706-00880.title: Cycle flow formulation of optimal network flow problems for centralized and decentralized solvers
arxiv-1706-00880.creator: Reza Asadi, Solmaz S. Kia
arxiv-1706-00880.description: Abstract When the underlying physical network layer in optimal network flow problems is a large graph, the associated optimization problem has a large set of decision variables. In this paper, we discuss how the cycle basis from graph theory can be used to reduce the size of this decision variable space.

arxiv-1902-02646.title: All Ramsey ( C n , K 6 ) (C_{n},K_{6}) critical graphs for large n n
arxiv-1902-02646.creator: C. J. Jayawardene
arxiv-1902-02646.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by C. J. Jayawardene. Let G G and H H be finite graphs without loops or multiple edges. If for any two-coloring of the edges of a complete graph K n K_{n} , there is a copy of G G in the first color, red, or a copy of H H in the second color, blue, we will say K n → ( G , H ) K_{n}\rightarrow(G,H) .

arxiv-2103-11295.title: A frequency quintupled laser at 308 nm for spectroscopy of intercombination lines in zinc
arxiv-2103-11295.creator: Maya Büki, David Röser and Simon Stellmer University of Bonn, Nussallee 12, 53115 Bonn, Germany
arxiv-2103-11295.description: Abstract Many experiments in atomic physics and quantum optics, among them optical atomic clocks, require laser sources in the ultra-violet wavelength range with very low intensity noise and phase noise. The development of such lasers is a challenge, especially when a robust and transportable system is required.

arxiv-2105-09520.title: Nullstellensatz for relative existentially closed groups
arxiv-2105-09520.creator: M. Shahryari
arxiv-2105-09520.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Shahryari. We prove that in every variety of G G -groups, every G G -existentially closed element satisfies nullstellensatz for finite consistent systems of equations. This will generalize Theorem G of [ 1 ] . As a result we see that every pair of G G -existentially closed elements in an arbitrary variety of G G -groups generate the same quasi-variety and if both of them are q ω q_{\omega} -compact, they are geometrically equivalent. AMS Subject Classification
Primary 20F70, Secondary 08A99.

arxiv-2201-00807.title: Einstein and the problem of confirmation by previously known evidence: A comment on Michel Janssen and Jürgen Renn’s Einstein and the Perihelion Motion of Mercury
arxiv-2201-00807.creator: Galina Weinstein
arxiv-2201-00807.description: Abstract In this paper, I comment on a recent paper by Michel Janssen and Jürgen Renn ( [ 24 ] ). In his published paper of November 18, 1915, Einstein presented a solution to the problem of the perihelion motion of Mercury and obtained the correct result of 43 seconds of arc per century.

arxiv-2204-12188.description: Abstract One the of the applications in the realm of the IoT ( IoT ) is real-time localization of assets in specific application environments where satellite based global positioning is unviable. Numerous approaches for localization relying on wireless sensor mesh systems have been evaluated, but the recent BLE ( BLE ) 5.

arxiv-2306-03714.title: DashQL – Complete Analysis Workflows with SQL
arxiv-2306-03714.creator: André Kohn, Dominik Moritz, Thomas Neumann
arxiv-2306-03714.description: Abstract We present DashQL, a language that describes complete analysis workflows in self-contained scripts. DashQL combines SQL, the grammar of relational database systems, with a grammar of graphics in a grammar of analytics. It supports preparing and visualizing arbitrarily complex SQL statements in a single coherent language.

arxiv-2401-07880.title: Existence and uniqueness of Monge minimizers for a Multi-marginal Optimal Transport problem with intermolecular interactions cost
arxiv-2401-07880.creator: Augusto Gerolin, Mircea Petrache, Adolfo Vargas-Jiménez
arxiv-2401-07880.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Augusto Gerolin, Mircea Petrache, Adolfo Vargas-Jiménez. We investigate a new multi-marginal optimal transport problem arising from a dissociation model in the Strong Interaction Limit of Density Functional Theory. In this short note, we introduce such dissociation model, the corresponding optimal transport problem as well as show preliminary results on the existence and uniqueness of Monge solutions assuming absolute continuity of at least two of the marginals. Finally, we show that such marginal regularity conditions are necessary for the existence of an unique Monge solution.

arxiv-2408-08413.title: Towards quantitative precision in functional QCD I
arxiv-2408-08413.creator: Friederike Ihssen, Jan M. Pawlowski, Franz R. Sattler, Nicolas Wink
arxiv-2408-08413.description: Abstract Functional approaches are the only first principle QCD setup that allow for direct computations at finite density. Predictive power and quantitative reliability of the respective results can only be obtained within a systematic expansion scheme with controlled systematic error estimates.

arxiv-2408-13912.title: Splatt3R: Zero-shot Gaussian Splatting from Uncalibrated Image Pairs
arxiv-2408-13912.creator: Brandon Smart, Chuanxia Zheng, Iro Laina, Victor Adrian Prisacariu
arxiv-2408-13912.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce Splatt3R, a pose-free, feed-forward method for in-the-wild 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis from stereo pairs. Given uncalibrated natural images, Splatt3R can predict 3D Gaussian Splats without requiring any camera parameters or depth information.

arxiv-2409-06142.title: Variational Search Distributions
arxiv-2409-06142.creator: Daniel M. Steinberg, Rafael Oliveira, Cheng Soon Ong & Edwin V. Bonilla
arxiv-2409-06142.description: Abstract We develop variational search distributions (VSD) , a method for conditioning a generative model of discrete, combinatorial designs on a rare desired class by efficiently evaluating a black-box (e.g. experiment, simulation) in a batch sequential manner. We call this task active generation; we formalize active generation’s requirements and desiderata, and formulate a solution via variational inference.

arxiv-2504-05385.title: Logarithmic angle-dependent gauge transformations at null infinity
arxiv-2504-05385.creator: Oscar Fuentealba, and Marc Henneaux
arxiv-2504-05385.description: Abstract Logarithmic angle-dependent gauge transformations are symmetries of electromagnetism that are canonically conjugate to the standard 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathcal{O}(1) angle-dependent u ⁡ ( 1 ) u(1) transformations. They were exhibited a few years ago at spatial infinity. In this paper, we derive their explicit form at null infinity.

arxiv-2509-03272.title: Amplified capture rate of dark matter in compact binaries and constraints on bosonic dark matter from GW170817
arxiv-2509-03272.creator: János Takátsy 1,2, Lorenz Zwick 1,2, David O’Neill 1, Johan Samsing 1,2
arxiv-2509-03272.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by János Takátsy 1,2, Lorenz Zwick 1,2, David O’Neill 1, Johan Samsing 1,2. The accretion of dark matter (DM) onto compact objects and the potential gravitational collapse of neutron stars due to this accretion has become a promising indirect probe of DM properties, complementing terrestrial experiments. We show that the accretion flux of DM on stellar objects is amplified in binary systems due to the complex gravitational interaction of said particles with the binary.

arxiv-2511-09857.title: On the structure of locally conformally flat orbifolds and ALE metrics
arxiv-2511-09857.creator: Xiaokang Wang
arxiv-2511-09857.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove several structure theorems for locally conformally flat, positive Yamabe orbifolds and nonnegative scalar curvature, ALE manifolds. These two kinds of spaces can be related by conformal blow-up and conformal compactification. For the orbifolds, we prove that such orbifolds admit a manifold cover.

arxiv-2603-08276.creator: Wenzhe Huang, Guochun Shen, Dingliang Xing, Jiangyan Zhao

pmc-10767828.creator: Varadi M, Bertoni D, Magana P et al.
pmc-10767828.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). The AlphaFold Database Protein Structure Database (AlphaFold DB, https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk ) has significantly impacted structural biology by amassing over 214 million predicted protein structures, expanding from the initial 300k structures released in 2021. Enabled by the grou

pmc-11436138.title: Model and Method for Providing Resilience to Resource-Constrained AI-System
pmc-11436138.creator: Viacheslav Moskalenko, Vyacheslav Kharchenko, Serhii Semenov
pmc-11436138.description: Artificial intelligence technologies are becoming increasingly prevalent in resource-constrained, safety-critical embedded systems. Numerous methods exist to enhance the resilience of AI systems against disruptive influences. However, when resources are limited, ensuring cost-effective resilience becomes crucial. A promising approach for reducing the resource consumption of AI systems during test-time involves applying the concepts and methods of dynamic neural networks.

pmc-11499634.title: Characterization of varietal effects on the acidity and pH of grape berries for selection of varieties better adapted to climate change
pmc-11499634.creator: Marc Plantevin, Yoann Merpault, Julien Lecourt, Agnès Destrac-Irvine, Lucile Dijsktra, Cornelis van Leeuwen
pmc-11499634.description: Climate change is drastically modifying berry composition and wine quality across the world. Most wine regions with a history of winemaking are suffering from a loss of typicity and terroir expression because of climate change impact on berry components at harvest, including wine acidity, with total acidity decreasing and pH increasing.

pmc-11628966.title: How often do parents administer medications to their children in hospital? A prospective direct observational study
pmc-11628966.creator: Johanna I Westbrook, Ling Li, Tim Badgery-Parker, Erin Fitzpatrick, Virginia Mumford, Alison Merchant, Magdalena Z Raban
pmc-11628966.description: Parents and carers play a critical role in supporting their children while in hospital. Multiple qualitative studies have explored parental involvement in the care of hospitalised children. Administration of medication to young children can be difficult and cause anxiety and stress for children.

pmc-11689268.title: EFFECTS OF HEARING INTERVENTION ON BRAIN HEALTH: FINDINGS OF THE ACHIEVE TRIAL AND AND ACHIEVE-MRI SUBSTUDY
pmc-11689268.creator: Alison Huang, Frank Lin, Caterina Rosano
pmc-11689268.description: This session will present the primary findings of the ACHIEVE-MRI (Aging and Cognitive Health Evaluation in Elders Magnetic Resonance Imaging) study, a substudy of the ACHIEVE randomized controlled trial (Clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT03243422). Prior observational studies have linked hearing loss with changes in brain structure and function.

pmc-11716537.title: Comparison of amyloid positron emission tomography, hippocampal volume, and plasma biomarkers in predicting conversion to mild cognitive impairment
pmc-11716537.creator: Murat Bilgel, Yang An, Ishaan Shah, Keenan A Walker, Abhay Moghekar, Nicholas J Ashton, Przemyslaw Radoslaw Kac, Thomas K Karikari, Kaj Blennow, Henrik Zetterberg, Madhav Thambisetty, Susan M Resnick
pmc-11716537.description: BackgroundWe examined whether brain amyloid PET, hippocampal volume, or plasma biomarkers are better predictors of conversion to mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodIn the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA), plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light chain (NfL) concentrations were measured using Quanterix Simoa Neurology 4‐plex E.

pmc-12540579.title: Understanding infant stress in neonatal and pediatric intensive care: a scoping review
pmc-12540579.creator: Christine Riley, Christopher Mastropietro, Ashley Darcy-Mahoney, Christine Pintz, Quiping Pearl Zhou, Pamela S Hinds
pmc-12540579.description: Infants in intensive care environments encounter numerous stressors which may overlap or occur in close proximity. Recent literature suggests stressful encounters in the neonatal or early infant period are harmful to physiological, functional, and structural systems, both acutely and longitudinally.

pmc-12557553.title: ViClickbait-2025: A comprehensive dataset for Vietnamese clickbait detection
pmc-12557553.creator: Dai Phuoc Nguyen, Thien Khai Tran, Y Minh Nguyen, Bay Vo
pmc-12557553.description: ViClickbait-2025 is a curated Vietnamese-language dataset developed to facilitate research on automatic clickbait detection. It comprises 3414 headline samples collected through web scraping from eight major Vietnamese online news platforms between 2023 and 2025. Each headline is annotated as either clickbait or non-clickbait, with 31.2 % labeled as clickbait.

pmc-13077027.title: 25 Years of “Loop” Radiochemistry for PET Imaging
pmc-13077027.creator: Emily Murrell, Sahil Khan, Neil Vasdev
pmc-13077027.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While conventional methods to 11C‐ and 18F‐labelled radiopharmaceuticals utilize a vial‐based approach, in the past quarter‐century, a modern, efficient, and cleaner “loop method” has been developed. This Perspective will shed light on the history behind the development of the loop radiochemistry method, the multifold advantages associated with the method over other approaches, its applications to the synthesis of 11C‐ and 18F‐labelled compounds and radiopharmaceuticals for preclinical and human PET imaging studies, its eventual expansion to diverse organic chemistry reactions and finally provide

pmc-13348749.title: Study of phosphorylated ribosomal protein S6 (pS6) in the clinical outcomes of patients undergoing hepatectomy for metastatic colorectal cancer
pmc-13348749.creator: Rafaella Henriques Cavalcanti Torres de Melo, Paulo Goberlianio de Barros Silva, Heladio Feitosa e Castro Neto, Rayane Cardoso de Souza Nunes, José Ricardo de Moura Torres de Melo, Maria Julia Barbosa Bezerra, Conceição Aparecida Dornelas, Carlos Gustavo Hirth

pmc-13421257.title: Establishing normal myocardial blood flow and myocardial flow reserve values: a rubidium-82 positron emission tomography study
pmc-13421257.creator: Martin Lyngby Lassen, Niels Høeg Brandt-Jacobsen, Piotr Slomka, Tine W. Hansen, Yeliz Bulut, Caroline Kistorp, Andreas Kjaer, Philip Hasbak
pmc-13421257.description: PurposeQuantitative Rubidium-82 (82Rb) PET allows assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF) and flow reserve (MFR), yet clinically applicable normal reference ranges remain incompletely defined across age and sex. This study aims to establish age- and sex-specific reference ranges for resting MBF (rMBF), stress MBF (sMBF), and MFR using 82Rb PET in healthy adults.

pmc-13612693.title: Intergenerational income mobility and psychotropic drug dispensation in a 1953 Stockholm cohort: a diagonal reference model approach
pmc-13612693.creator: Klara Gurzo, Anna Oksuzyan, Bitte Modin
pmc-13612693.description: The theoretical link between intergenerational social mobility and mental health has long been explored in the social sciences. Declining social mobility in high-income countries alongside rising mental health concerns have reignited interest in this research area. Sweden, while experiencing similar trends, remains a country known for its high social mobility.

pmc-13630657.title: The predictive value of aGAPSS score combined with clinical factors for thrombosis in systemic lupus erythematosus
pmc-13630657.creator: Juan Shi, Libo Ouyang, Qiong Ma, Peiming Zheng
pmc-13630657.description: PurposeThis study evaluated the predictive value of antiphospholipid antibodies (aPLs) combined with the adjusted global antiphospholipid syndrome score (aGAPSS) for thrombosis in hospitalized systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients.MethodsA retrospective analysis included 309 SLE patients (65 with in-hospital thrombosis, 244 without). Demographic, clinical, and serological data were collected.
